newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Vietnamese puppeteers seek Australia asylum-newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Vietnamese puppeteers seek Australia asylum-newspaper.

text.p: A troupe of Vietnamese water puppeteers who fear persecution at home for performing with Western artists has asked for refugee status in Australia, an Australian newspaper reported on Friday.
However, Australia's immigration department was unable to confirm whether the seven members of the Hanoi-based Song Ngoc Water Puppet Theatre group had sought asylum.
"With any application, our hands are tied when it comes to personal information about people," an immigration department spokesman told Reuters.

The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper reported on Friday that the puppeteers, who were due to return to Vietnam last month after arriving in Australia in December, were living in a rented house in western Sydney.
The newspaper said the puppeteers had been granted bridging visas while their applications for refugee status were being processed.
"If we have to return to Vietnam, we would rather die here," said troupe manager Anh Bich Luong in the newspaper. "In Vietnam, you can be jailed up to 15 years for writing a poem."

Hung Van Nhu, another spokesman for the group, said the Vietnamese government wanted to stop them from working with Australian performers because secrets of the 1,000-year-old art of a water puppetry might be revealed.
He said Vietnamese authorities were upset because the performers had come in contact with foreigners and because they consider water puppetry to be a national cultural asset.
